report.summary: Checkout service experienced a 503 acquisition timeout at 14:10 after pool exhaustion (all 20 connections occupied). Inventory latency increased from 180ms to 6200ms at 14:08, temporally preceding the pool exhaustion. The checkout failure mechanism is pool exhaustion with timeout; however, the root cause of elevated inventory latency and connection holdover remains unexplained due to missing inventory-service logs and metrics.
uncertainties: Root cause of inventory latency spike (6200ms at 14:08) is unknown: no inventory-service logs, database metrics, or downstream dependency health data supplied.
Whether inventory latency directly caused connection holdover or whether a separate upstream event triggered both symptoms.
No metrics after 14:10 supplied; unclear if pool exhaustion persisted, when it resolved, or if inventory latency recovered.
No checkout request volume or error rate data provided; unable to quantify impact or distinguish spike from sustained degradation.
recommendations: Obtain inventory-service application logs from 14:00–14:15 to identify queries, errors, or resource contention at 14:08.
Provide inventory-service backend metrics (CPU, memory, database connection pool status, query execution times) for 14:00–14:15.
Supply checkout-service connection pool metrics (in-use, wait queue depth, acquisition latency) from 14:00–14:15 to confirm recovery and identify cascade timing.
Retrieve upstream dependencies (database, cache, external APIs) health and latency metrics at 14:08 to isolate the inventory latency source.
Request checkout error logs and request volume (14:00–14:15) to correlate pool exhaustion with traffic load or retry behavior.

findings.statement: Checkout service pool exhaustion occurred at 14:10 with all 20 connections occupied, triggering 503 acquisition timeout.

findings.statement: Pool exhaustion is the checkout failure mechanism: elevated inventory response times likely caused connections to remain occupied longer than normal, preventing pool recycling.
